discrepancy.plain_explanation: The hospital bill asks for $466.00. Medicare's own notice for the same visit says the most the hospital may bill you is $226.00. The difference is exactly $240.00, which is line 3 on the bill: the contrast dye used for the CT scan. Medicare treats that dye as part of the CT scan payment, so it shows $0.00 as your share. It looks like the hospital's billing system passed that $240.00 on to you instead of writing it off. This is worth asking the hospital to correct before the Nov 30 due date.
evidence: Bill line 3 (Q9967, contrast material, charge $240.00) ↔ MSN line 3 (Q9967): approved $0.00, Medicare paid $0.00, 'you may be billed' $0.00, note: payment included in another service.
Bill 'patient owes' $466.00 (statement 2026-10-20, account ****4821) ↔ MSN 'Maximum you may be billed' $226.00 for the same date of service 2026-09-14.

Bill lines 1, 2, 4, 5 ↔ MSN lines 1, 2, 4, 5: each bill charge matches the MSN 'amount facility charged' to the cent, and 20% of each approved amount ($84 + $93 + $30 + $19) sums to the MSN total $226.00.
$466.00 − $226.00 = $240.00 = bill line 3 charge (no other line can explain the gap).
discrepancy.uncertainty: This is a strong match, not proof. The MSN reflects the claim as processed on 2026-10-02; if the hospital later submitted a corrected claim, Medicare's figures could change. The bill is a summary statement, so the $240.00 is inferred from the totals gap matching line 3 exactly rather than from a per-line patient-responsibility column. The hospital may also have a reason we cannot see (for example a non-covered-item notice signed at the visit). The app therefore asks the hospital to review and explain, rather than asserting an overcharge.
discrepancy.rule_basis: Under Medicare's hospital outpatient prospective payment system, contrast agents such as Q9967 are packaged (payment status indicator N): their payment is included in the payment for the primary procedure, so there is no separate Medicare-approved amount and no separate patient coinsurance. A participating hospital accepting Medicare assignment may collect only the deductible and coinsurance Medicare calculates on approved amounts, which the MSN states as 'Maximum you may be billed'. Billing the beneficiary for a packaged item on top of that is not permitted. Synthetic demo: verify the current status indicator for Q9967 in the CMS Addendum B at build time.

income.source: Typed by caregiver Jenna Hale at setup (no document uploaded): Social Security $2,050/month + pension $1,080/month = $3,130/month × 12 = $37,560/year. Unverified self-report; the hospital may ask for proof.

fap_policy.fpl_basis_note: Uses the 2025 HHS poverty guideline for a 1-person household in the 48 contiguous states: $15,650 (published January 2025). The 2026 guideline is normally published in January 2026 and MUST be verified and swapped in at build time (one constant, FPL_1_PERSON). The FAP tiers are the synthetic demo partner's policy, not any real hospital's.

assistance.status_label: Estimated — appears to fall in the 75% discount tier (240% of FPL). Not confirmed by the hospital; applied to the corrected balance of $226.00, not to the $466.00 billed.

proposed_actions.title: Ask Patient Financial Services to remove the $240.00 contrast charge
proposed_actions.summary: Points the hospital to MSN line 3, asks for a corrected statement and a hold on the account while they review. Caregiver reads, can edit, then taps Approve to send. Nothing is sent before the tap.
proposed_actions.draft_excerpt: To: Patient Financial Services, Riverbend Community Hospital. Re: account ending 4821, statement dated October 20, 2026, service date September 14, 2026, patient Dorothy Hale. The statement asks for $466.00. Medicare's Summary Notice for the same visit says the most I may be billed is $226.00. The $240.00 difference is line 3 on the statement (Q9967, contrast material). The Medicare notice shows this item as included in the payment for the CT scan, with $0.00 patient responsibility. Please review the account, remove the $240.00 if it was billed to me in error, send a corrected statement, and place the account on hold until this is resolved. If you believe the charge is correct, please explain why in writing. — Jenna Hale, authorized representative for Dorothy Hale (authorization attached).

proposed_actions.title: Apply for the hospital's financial assistance program
proposed_actions.summary: Pre-fills the demo partner's FAP form from the income typed at setup. Asks the hospital to apply its 75% tier to the corrected balance. Caregiver confirms the income figure and taps Approve. Eligibility is the hospital's decision.
proposed_actions.draft_excerpt: I am applying for financial assistance for Dorothy Hale, account ending 4821. Household size: 1. Annual income: $37,560 (Social Security and a pension). That is about 240% of the federal poverty guideline. Under your published Financial Assistance Policy this appears to fall in the 75% discount tier. Please apply the discount to the balance after the correction requested separately is processed. I can provide income documents on request. I understand the hospital decides eligibility. — Jenna Hale, authorized representative.

simulated_response.text: SYNTHETIC — simulated letter from Riverbend Community Hospital Patient Financial Services, dated 2026-11-21. 'Re: account ending 4821. We reviewed your request of November 9. Line Q9967 (contrast material, $240.00) is packaged with the CT scan under Medicare outpatient payment rules and should not have been billed to the patient. We have removed it; the corrected patient balance is $226.00. Your financial assistance application was approved at the 75% tier (household income at 240% of the federal poverty guideline). A discount of $169.50 has been applied. Your new balance is $56.50, due December 21, 2026. No collection activity occurred during review.'

outcome.basis: SYNTHETIC. Estimated opportunity ($240.00 discrepancy + $169.50 estimated FAP reduction = $409.50) was computed by the app before any response. Confirmed adjustment ($240.00 removed + $169.50 discount = $409.50) comes from the simulated hospital letter dated 2026-11-21. Patient savings equals the confirmed adjustment because the patient had been asked to pay $466.00 and had paid nothing: $466.00 − $56.50 = $409.50. The three numbers happen to match in this demo; the app still tracks them separately because the hospital's answer often differs from the estimate.
